claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline alloy has high density.
The baseline alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility.
The baseline alloy exhibits brittle inter-crystalline fracture.
Adding 1-3 at.% Si and aging will precipitate silicide intermetallic phases in the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr BCC matrix.
The precipitates will include Hf5Si3 or (Hf,Zr)Si2.
The silicides will form a discontinuous reticulated network along grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
Aging at 800-1000 °C can control silicide nucleation and growth sufficiently to produce the proposed morphology.
A discontinuous reticulated silicide network will arrest and deflect propagating cracks.
Crack deflection will increase fracture-surface area and promote localized plasticity in the BCC matrix.
The proposed phase morphology will improve room-temperature ductility and fracture toughness relative to the single-phase baseline.
Yield strength will be maintained or slightly reduced because of a softening effect associated with the phase distribution.
Si addition and silicide formation will cause a density increase of less than 1%.
Typical RHEAs with a continuous ordered B2 matrix exhibit poor room-temperature ductility.
Intrinsically brittle silicide, B2, and Laves secondary phases can limit ambient-temperature tensile ductility in refractory HEAs.
Keeping the silicide volume fraction low will avoid embrittlement while retaining the proposed crack-deflection benefit.
Above approximately 5 at.% Si, silicides may become continuous or form large brittle particles and cause severe embrittlement.
The proposed operating regime is room-temperature uniaxial compression at 25 °C.
A 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, and 7 at.% Si series aged at 900 °C for 24 hours provides a baseline control and composition-dependent test.

The hypothesis is falsified if 1-3 at.% Si produces the proposed silicides but ductility improves by less than 5%, or if the silicides have a continuous or large-isolated-particle morphology rather than a reticulated network.
